The well was originally the sole water supply for the Indian reserve but was replaced by WTNs 112411 and 117854.  From the WWA report: 

    "The first groundwater source for the MLIB I.R.#1 community was drilled in 1977 (referred to in this report and other reports as PW77-1) This well is located east of the main community, on a bench above McLeod Lake, which is 100 m further east. A report documenting the completion of PW77-1 was not available, but information on this well is first provided in a report by Golder Associates (1985). PW77-1 was reportedly 18.5 m deep, with 1.5 m of 30 slot screen over the deepest 1.5 m of the well. As reported in Golder (1985), this well was originally test pumped at 21 US gpm for 12 hours, with 1.98 m of drawdown. In 1982, the yield available from the well reportedly dropped to 12 US gpm, suspected to be the result of screen siltation."

Later in the WWA report  it states:
    "While onsite, it was reported that a former well was located in a manhole somewhere near PW86-1 (WTN 117854). The lid of the manhole was located but could not be opened. After a more thorough review of previous reports, it appears the well in the manhole is actually PW77-1. This well still requires closure, which can likely be done in concert with installation of the permanent pump in PW15-01 (WTN 112411)".

Historical geological borehole record TR-16. The supplied log pages document geological strata extending to 400 ft, including sandstone, shale, coal, bony coal and trap rock.

The lower log records brown and black shale, coal-bearing intervals, coarse-grain sandstone and a final 7-ft trap-rock interval from 393 to 400 ft. The recorded depth/elevation figures imply a historical reference elevation of 793 ft, with the datum unconfirmed.

The supplied pages do not show the original record header or complete upper geological section. Some previously transcribed intervals, including the thin coal/shale beds between 161 and 190 ft, require verification against the missing upper log.

No drilling method, casing details, groundwater measurements, pumping tests or water-quality results are recorded in the supplied pages.

The address and postal code (V0R 1W0) are placeholders used to meet GWELLS requirements. The exact civic address and coordinates are unverified.
